name: Lexapro vs Zoloft
title: Lexapro vs Zoloft: Differences, Similarities & Which Is Better
description: Compare Lexapro (escitalopram) and Zoloft (sertraline) - two commonly prescribed SSRIs for depression and anxiety. Learn about effectiveness, side effects, dosing, and which might be right for you.

summary.bottom_line: Both Lexapro and Zoloft are effective SSRIs for treating depression and anxiety. Lexapro is often considered slightly better tolerated with fewer drug interactions, while Zoloft has a broader FDA-approved indication list and more flexibility in dosing.

Weight neutral to slight loss initially

sections.heading: Lexapro vs Zoloft: Overview
sections.content: Lexapro (escitalopram) and Zoloft (sertraline) are both selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), the most commonly prescribed class of antidepressants. Both work by increasing serotonin levels in the brain, improving mood, reducing anxiety, and helping regulate sleep and appetite. While they share the same mechanism, there are important differences in their side effect profiles, drug interactions, and FDA-approved uses.

sections.heading: Which Is More Effective?
sections.content: Clinical studies show both medications are similarly effective for treating depression and anxiety. A large meta-analysis found escitalopram (Lexapro) had a slight edge in efficacy among SSRIs, but the difference is small. In practice, individual response varies significantly - some patients do better on one than the other. If one doesn't work well, switching to the other is a reasonable approach.

sections.heading: Side Effects Comparison
sections.content: Both medications share common SSRI side effects including nausea, headache, insomnia, sexual dysfunction, and drowsiness. However, there are notable differences:

subsections.heading: Lexapro tends to have
items: Lower rates of GI upset (nausea, diarrhea)
Potentially more weight gain over time

subsections.heading: Zoloft tends to have
items: Higher rates of diarrhea and GI symptoms
Slightly more drug interactions due to CYP2D6 effects

sections.heading: Drug Interactions
sections.content: Lexapro has fewer drug interactions because it has minimal effects on cytochrome P450 enzymes. Zoloft moderately inhibits CYP2D6, which can affect levels of other medications including some beta-blockers, antipsychotics, and pain medications. Both interact dangerously with MAOIs and should not be combined with other serotonergic drugs without medical supervision (risk of serotonin syndrome).

subsections.heading: Pregnancy & Breastfeeding
subsections.content: Zoloft is generally considered the preferred SSRI during pregnancy due to more safety data. Both pass into breast milk but are generally considered compatible with breastfeeding.

subsections.heading: Children & Adolescents
subsections.content: Zoloft is FDA-approved for OCD in children 6+ and is commonly used off-label for pediatric depression and anxiety. Lexapro is approved for depression in adolescents 12+.

subsections.heading: Elderly
subsections.content: Both are used in older adults. Lower starting doses are recommended. Watch for hyponatremia (low sodium) with either medication.

sections.heading: Switching Between Lexapro and Zoloft
sections.content: If one SSRI isn't working well or causes intolerable side effects, switching to another is common practice. Your doctor may do a direct switch (stopping one and starting the other) or a cross-taper (gradually reducing one while starting the other). Never stop an antidepressant abruptly without medical guidance.

sections.heading: Cost Comparison
sections.content: Both medications are available as generics and are similarly affordable. Generic escitalopram and sertraline typically cost $4-$30/month depending on pharmacy and insurance. Brand-name versions are significantly more expensive and rarely necessary.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: There's no universally "better" choice - it depends on your specific situation:

recommendations.when: You want fewer drug interactions, are sensitive to GI side effects, or prefer once-daily simplicity
You're pregnant or planning pregnancy, need treatment for OCD/PTSD/panic, or prefer more dosing flexibility
You have uncomplicated depression or GAD with no strong preference factors

faqs.a: Neither is inherently "stronger." Lexapro is more potent milligram-for-milligram (10-20mg vs 50-200mg), but this just reflects dosing differences, not effectiveness. Both achieve similar therapeutic effects at their standard doses.

faqs.q: Which causes less weight gain - Lexapro or Zoloft?
faqs.a: Zoloft may cause slightly less weight gain than Lexapro. Some studies show sertraline is weight-neutral or even associated with modest weight loss initially, while escitalopram is more often associated with gradual weight gain over time.

faqs.q: Can I switch from Lexapro to Zoloft?
faqs.a: Yes, switching between SSRIs is common when one isn't working well. Your doctor will guide the transition - either a direct switch or gradual cross-taper. Never stop an antidepressant without medical supervision.
Lexapro is often considered slightly better tolerated overall, with lower rates of GI side effects and drug interactions. However, individual responses vary significantly.

Both are effective for anxiety. Zoloft has more FDA-approved anxiety indications (panic, PTSD, social anxiety), while Lexapro is approved for GAD. In practice, both work well for most anxiety disorders.
